name: sexual health overview
title: Approach to a sexual health concern: know your biases, ask permission and take the CDC 5 P's, then the Pleasure questions place the concern in a phase of the response cycle (desire, arousal, orgasm and resolution) or outside it (pain, illness, trauma); each column gives the question to ask, what is normal in both sexes, and how women and men differ

root.title: A sexual health concern: take the history, then find the PHASE it affects
lines: STEP ONE: know your own implicit biases before you walk in · stay NONJUDGMENTAL, whatever they admit to
ask PERMISSION, proactively · confidentiality early · open questions, silence, REPETITION to unpack a euphemism ("I think I need a check up")
CDC 5 P's: Partners · Practices · Protection + Past sexually transmitted infections · Pregnancy plans · ± Pleasure

groups.title: A PHASE of the response cycle: the PLEASURE questions find it
lines: Masters + Johnson: excitement → plateau → orgasm → resolution · Kaplan: sexual drive → excitement → orgasm

groups.title: NOT a phase
lines: pain is one of the Pleasure questions

head: h
Desire
Kaplan put it first
ask: Interest in sex, or a lack of it?
"Any change in your (or your partner's) desire, or how often you have sex?"
norm: • INHIBITORY: prolactin, serotonin at 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) 2 + 3 receptors, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)
sex: Women: desire need not come FIRST
most widely used model (Basson), a circle: arousal can TRIGGER desire
What turns women and men on differs
cultural expectations play a large role

head: h
Arousal
excitement + plateau
ask: Difficulty with lubrication? Getting or keeping an erection?
erectile dysfunction: one of the two commonest concerns in men
norm: • nitric oxide (NO): the major neurotransmitter of clitoral engorgement
• ↑ muscle tension (myotonia), heart rate, blood pressure
sex: • seeing or feeling their own arousal matters less

head: h
Orgasm + resolution
ask: premature ejaculation: the other commonest concern in men
norm: • still possible after a COMPLETE spinal cord injury
sex: no other orgasm or ejaculation possible during it

head: h
Pain or an illness
ask: "Many people are concerned about how this condition might affect their sex life. What is your experience?"
norm: Their answer decides what you offer
information on the illness and sexual function
sex: Men: especially likely to feel ashamed
allow time: 45–60 minutes is ideal, or book a LONGER visit

panels.title: Make the office a safe space
items: gender identity, pronouns and sexual preference as ROUTINE intake-form questions
two-step method: ask gender identity AND sex assigned at birth
staff trained in culturally sensitive terms · gender-inclusive forms · diverse images
adverse childhood experiences (sexual abuse, trauma) can make the topic hard to discuss
